questions.q: What is Snowflake Cortex, as described in this lesson?
options: A set of hosted LLMs you call from SQL or Python, with no separate model or GPU to deploy
A standalone AI application you install outside of Snowflake
A BI dashboard tool bundled with Snowflake
A dedicated GPU cluster the customer must provision and manage
questions.explain: Cortex functions are called like any other SQL function — Snowflake manages the hosted models behind the scenes.

questions.q: Which function family is the current, canonical surface for Cortex LLM calls as of 2026?
options: The AI_* family, such as AI_COMPLETE and AI_SUMMARIZE
The LEGACY_* family
The CORTEX_ONLY family
There is no naming convention; function names vary per account
questions.explain: Snowflake's AI_* (AISQL) functions — AI_COMPLETE, AI_SUMMARIZE, AI_SENTIMENT, AI_TRANSLATE, AI_EXTRACT, and others — are the current recommended surface.

questions.q: What does this lesson say about the older SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX.COMPLETE-style function names?
options: They still run today for backward compatibility, but are slated for deprecation by the end of 2026
They were removed entirely in 2025 and no longer run
They are the only names that have ever existed — AI_COMPLETE does not exist
They require a separate paid add-on to use
questions.explain: The legacy SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX.* names still work but Snowflake has said they'll be deprecated by the end of 2026 in favor of the AI_* family.

questions.q: According to this lesson, how are Cortex LLM function calls billed?
options: Metered by tokens processed by the model, on top of whatever warehouse is running the query
They are always free regardless of usage
A flat monthly fee per Snowflake account, unrelated to usage
Billed only by storage consumed, never by compute
questions.explain: Cortex functions consume credits based on token volume processed, in addition to normal warehouse billing.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say understanding AI_COMPLETE matters before the rest of Chapter 16?
options: Because Cortex Analyst, Cortex Search, and Cortex Agents are all built on these same LLM functions, with more structure layered on top
Because AI_COMPLETE is unrelated to any other Cortex feature
Because Cortex Agents replace the need for any LLM function entirely
Because Cortex Search does not use any LLM functions at all
questions.explain: Cortex Analyst, Search, and Agents are all built using these same hosted LLM functions plus a semantic model, search index, or orchestration loop on top.
